name: Glasp
why_listed: Readers and learners who want to highlight and annotate web pages, PDFs and YouTube transcripts, get AI summaries and push highlights into Obsidian or Notion would use Glasp instead of Spoken Margins.

platforms.value: iOS, iPadOS, Android, web, browser extensions (Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox and other Chromium browsers)
platforms.detail: Browser extension is the core; web app; iPhone/iPad and Android apps with a Safari extension on iOS.

sources.title: Download Glasp Mobile App for Free on iOS & Android | Glasp
sources.quote: Glasp runs on iPhone, iPad, and Android phones and tablets.

sources.title: FAQs (Glasp)
sources.quote: The Glasp Web Highlighter works on Chrome, Safari, Edge, Brave, Firefox, and Opera, as well as other Chromium-based browsers.

sources.quote: Requires iPadOS 15.1 or later.

plays_podcasts.detail: Not a podcast player; podcast highlights come in only through the separate Snipd app.

export_markdown_pkm.detail: Exports to Notion, Obsidian (official plugin), Readwise and others; Markdown download on every plan.

share_note_at_moment.detail: Highlights are public by default and appear to other readers on the same page; a Community tab lets them tap a passage to jump to it. Text only, no audio moments beyond YouTube timestamps on one's own highlights.

share_note_at_moment.note: Sharing is via the public Glasp layer, not a file another person imports.

group_listening.detail: Social layer (public highlights, following, community feed) but no private groups.

on_device_privacy.detail: Cloud service tied to an account; highlights are public by default and private highlights are a Pro feature.

sources.title: FAQs (Glasp)

on_device_privacy.note: Rated no: highlights are stored in Glasp's cloud under an account, and are public by default.

account_required.detail: Sign-up is via Google or Apple; highlights sync to the account.

account_required.note: Since iOS 3.11.0 the Safari button appears before sign-in, but saving highlights is account-based.
